newsitem.title: UK: William Cook rejects new Triplex bid.
newsitem.headline: William Cook rejects new Triplex bid.

text.p: British steel products group William Cook Plc said on Tuesday it rejected a higher takeover bid from British engineering group Triplex Lloyd Plc.

"Neither Triplex Lloyd's new offer nor its old arguments are convincing...its offer may no longer be ludicrously low but it remains manifestly low," Andrew Cook, chairman of William Cook said in a statement.

Earlier on Tuesday Triplex said it raised its bid for William Cook to 400.7p per share, which it said valued the steel products group's issued ordinary share capital at around 74.8 million pounds. Its previous offer valued William Cook at just under 58 million pounds and was worth around 309p per share.

William Cook said the new offer undervalued the company and failed to take into account "substantially" increased profits in the current year, the imminent completion of its modernisation programme and its growth prospects.
It said the Triplex bid valued each William Cook share at 389.1p based on a mid-market price of 192.5p per Triplex share, down 11p from 203.5p before the new bid was announced.
Triplex was down 11p at 192.5p on Tuesday morning.
Triplex said earlier on Tuesday its increased offer was final and would be made on the basis of 21 new Triplex shares and 3,740 pence in cash for every 20 William Cook shares.
Triplex, which launched its bid in November, was previously offering seven of its own shares and 1350 pence cash for every nine William Cook shares.
